title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
pattern: Divide and Conquer on Tree Traversals
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<int,int> idx: up to n entries → O(n)
- recursion call stack: worst case O(n) for a skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced
- int preIdx, int n: O(1)
- not counted: input arrays preorder/inorder, returned tree nodes
approach: The first element of preorder is always the current subtree's root. Find that root's position in inorder using a hash map (O(1) lookup); everything to its left is the left subtree, everything to its right is the right subtree. Recurse, advancing a global preorder index each time a root is consumed - this naturally matches preorder's root-left-right order. The hash map avoids O(n) linear search per node, giving linear total time.
hints: Where does the first preorder element appear in the inorder array, and what do the elements on each side of it represent? All values are unique.

Use a hash map storing each value's index in inorder. Example: preorder = [3,9,20,15,7], inorder = [9,3,15,20,7]. Root 3 sits at index 1 in inorder, so left subtree = inorder[0..0], right subtree = inorder[2..4].

```
build(lo, hi):
    if lo > hi: return null
    rootVal = preorder[preIdx++]
    mid = indexMap[rootVal]
    root = new Node(rootVal)
    root.left  = build(lo, mid - 1)
    root.right = build(mid + 1, hi)
    return root
```

**Single node** - n = 1, the minimum input size.
`Input: preorder = [-1], inorder = [-1]` → `Expected: [-1]`
⚠️ Bug: using `lo >= hi` as the base case → returns `[]`

**Right-skewed tree** - every node has only a right child.
`Input: preorder = [1,2,3], inorder = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: [1,null,2,null,3]`
⚠️ Bug: using `lo >= hi` as the base case → returns `[1,null,2]`

**Left-skewed tree** - every node has only a left child.
`Input: preorder = [3,2,1], inorder = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: [3,2,1]`
⚠️ Bug: swapping the recursive ranges (`root->right = build(lo, mid-1)`, `root->left = build(mid+1, hi)`) → returns `[3,null,2,null,1]`

**Searching the wrong array** - root lookup done in preorder instead of inorder.
`Input: preorder = [1,2,3], inorder = [2,1,3]` → `Expected: [1,2,3]`
⚠️ Bug: building the index map from preorder instead of inorder → returns `[1,null,2,null,3]`

followUps.q: Construct the tree from postorder and inorder traversal instead.
followUps.a: Same divide-and-conquer pattern, but the root is the last element of postorder. Consume postorder from right to left, and recurse the right subtree before the left subtree (since postorder is left-right-root). TC: O(n), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: Construct from preorder and postorder when the tree is a full binary tree.
followUps.a: The root is the first element of preorder and the last of postorder. The second preorder element is the left child's root; find it in postorder to determine the split point. This only works for full binary trees because a node with one child creates ambiguity. TC: O(n), SC: O(n).

Use an explicit stack. Push preorder nodes onto the stack; when the stack top matches the current inorder element, pop and advance the inorder pointer, then attach the next preorder node as a right child. TC: O(n), SC: O(n) for the stack.
